# [AMD] Enable mixed wave32/wave64 ROCm AOT kernels

## Summary

Enable `sgl_kernel` builds for `gfx1100` and `gfx1201`, including mixed CDNA/RDNA binaries.

The optimized MoE TopK launchers previously used wave64 in ROCm host code while gfx11/gfx12 device code used wave32. This made host launch geometry disagree with the compiled kernel. This PR builds explicit 32- and 64-lane variants and selects the correct one from the current device at runtime.

## Changes

- Add `gfx1100` and `gfx1201` to the `setup_rocm.py` target allowlist. Existing semicolon-separated `AMDGPU_TARGET` handling produces the fat binary.
- Read the current device's cached `warpSize` through `at::cuda::getCurrentDeviceProperties()`.
- Template softmax and sigmoid TopK kernels, constants, launch bounds, grid calculations, and block dimensions on `WARP_SIZE_PARAM`.
- Dispatch `<32>` on wave32 devices and `<64>` on wave64 devices. CUDA keeps its existing 32-lane path.
- Compile QuickReduce placeholders on gfx11/gfx12 while preserving the real implementation on CDNA. Runtime QuickReduce remains restricted to gfx94/gfx95.
- Keep custom and deterministic all-reduce compiled and registered for mixed binaries.

## Additional changes (rebased onto current `amd_march`)

- `setup_rocm.py`: `gfx1151` (RDNA3.5 / Strix Halo, also wave32) is added to the supported targets alongside `gfx1100` and `gfx1201`.
- `kvcacheio/transfer.cu`: block size on ROCm now uses the device wave size (`get_current_warp_size()`) instead of the host-side `WARP_SIZE`, which is always 64.
- Removed `docker/patches/sgl-kernel-gfx1151.sh` and its step in `docker/rocm-gfx1151.Dockerfile`. The patch lifted the arch gate and forced `WARP_SIZE=32` for gfx1151; both are now handled in-tree (allowlist + runtime wave-size dispatch).
- The MoE TopK fix also applies to `gfx1250`, which is wave32 and already a supported target.

Multi-arch (fat-binary) builds come from #44308. This PR's runtime wave-size dispatch works with it. Whichever merges second needs to add the RDNA targets to #44308's `supported_archs` list.

## Why runtime and compile-time selection are both needed

HIP builds one architecture-neutral host library and one device code object per `--offload-arch`. The host must inspect the executing GPU at runtime, while values used in `__launch_bounds__` and row-partition calculations must remain compile-time constants.

For example:

```text
gfx950  -> HIP selects gfx950 code object  -> warpSize=64 -> launch <64>
gfx1201 -> HIP selects gfx1201 code object -> warpSize=32 -> launch <32>
```

Using one `WARP_SIZE_PARAM` for both host geometry and device calculations keeps them consistent.

## Scope

This PR enables BF16/FP16 AOT operation and wave32 MoE routing on consumer RDNA. It does not enable native FP8 or DeepSeek-V4 FP8 support on gfx1100.

The existing `FP8_TYPE` compatibility block in `utils.h` is unchanged. Its type aliases describe FP8 representation for existing code; they are not a declaration that gfx1100 supports native FP8 computation. Native-FP8 kernels must continue to use their existing architecture capability gates or software fallbacks.

## Validation

Completed:

- Built and imported `sgl_kernel` on gfx1100 and gfx1201.
- Confirmed PyTorch reports wave size 32 on both systems.
- Ran end-to-end dense and MoE model paths on gfx1201 and gfx1100:

*gfx1201*:
| Model | TP | GSM8K accuracy | Invalid | GSM8K latency (s) | GSM8K output throughput (tok/s) | Serving output throughput (tok/s) | Serving total throughput (tok/s) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B` | 1 | 0.880 | 0.000 | 29.110 | 190.688 | 321.05 | 803.03 |
| `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B` | 4 | 0.640 | 0.000 | 30.845 | Not recorded | 707.03 | 1768.48 |
| `openai/gpt-oss-20b` | 2 | 0.620 | 0.120 | 41.000 | 536.194 | 686.22 | 1697.85 |

| `zai-org/GLM-4.7-Flash` | 4 | 0.180 | 0.000 | 95.892 | 153.662 | 463.45 | 1143.99 |
| `google/gemma-4-12b-it` | 2 | 0.440 | 0.020 | 82.347 | 161.863 | 466.66 | 1173.24 |

*gfx1100*:

| `zai-org/GLM-4.7-Flash` | 4 | 0.220 | 0.000 | 117.371 | 121.717 | 356.80 | 880.73 |

@@ -1,90 +0,0 @@
-#!/bin/sh
-# Teach python/sglang/kernels/aot/setup_rocm.py to build for gfx1151 (Strix Halo).
-# Applied at image-build time by docker/rocm-gfx1151.Dockerfile; the repo files are
-# left untouched because gfx1151 is not a supported SGLang target.
-#
-# Two changes:
-#   1. Lift the {gfx942, gfx950, gfx1250} allowlist, which otherwise sys.exit(1)s.
-#      Current main gives non-gfx942 targets a 40KB TopK dynamic-LDS budget,
-#      which already fits gfx1151's 64KB workgroup limit.
-#   2. Force a single WARP_SIZE across the host and device compiler passes.
-#      include/utils.h resolves WARP_SIZE to 64 whenever __HIP_DEVICE_COMPILE__
-#      is undefined -- i.e. on the host pass -- and to 32 on a non-__GFX9__
-#      device pass. On CDNA both come out 64 and nothing is wrong, which is why
-#      upstream never sees this. On gfx1151 the two passes disagree, and the MoE
-#      TopK kernels use WARP_SIZE on both sides of the launch:
-#         moe_topk_softmax_kernels.cu  __launch_bounds__(WARPS_PER_CTA * WARP_SIZE)  -> device, 4*32 = 128
-#         moe_topk_softmax_kernels.cu  dim3 block_dim(WARP_SIZE, WARPS_PER_TB)       -> host,   64*4 = 256
-#      Launching 256 threads into a 128-thread bound fails with
-#      hipErrorLaunchFailure, poisons the queue, and typically surfaces as a
-#      page fault in whatever kernel runs next (moe_align_block_size_kernel),
-#      which makes it easy to misattribute. The same pattern is in
-#      moe_topk_sigmoid_kernels.cu. It also desynchronizes the launcher's
-#      TopkConstants math (ROWS_PER_WARP, VECs_PER_THREAD) from the kernel's.
-#      Only MoE models hit this; dense models never call these kernels.
-#      32 is simply correct here -- gfx1151 is a wave32 part -- so the override
-#      pins both passes to 32 rather than renaming the symbol per call site.
-#
-# Each edit is guarded: if the upstream line has changed, fail rather than
-# silently produce an image whose kernels were built with the wrong limits.
-set -e
-
-FILE="${1:?usage: sgl-kernel-gfx1151.sh <path to setup_rocm.py>}"
-UTILS="$(dirname "${FILE}")/include/utils.h"
-
-GATE_OLD='if amdgpu_target not in ["gfx942", "gfx950", "gfx1250"]:'
-GATE_NEW='if amdgpu_target not in ["gfx942", "gfx950", "gfx1250", "gfx1151"]:'
-
-FLAGS_OLD='    f"-DSGL_TOPK_DYNAMIC_SMEM_BYTES={topk_dynamic_smem_bytes}",'
-FLAGS_NEW='    f"-DSGL_TOPK_DYNAMIC_SMEM_BYTES={topk_dynamic_smem_bytes}",
-    # gfx1151 is wave32; pin both compiler passes to it (see utils.h below).
-    *(["-DSGL_ROCM_WARP_SIZE=32"] if amdgpu_target == "gfx1151" else []),'
-
-WARP_OLD='#if defined(__GFX9__) || !defined(__HIP_DEVICE_COMPILE__)
-#define WARP_SIZE 64'
-WARP_NEW='#if defined(SGL_ROCM_WARP_SIZE)
-#define WARP_SIZE SGL_ROCM_WARP_SIZE
-#elif defined(__GFX9__) || !defined(__HIP_DEVICE_COMPILE__)
-#define WARP_SIZE 64'
-
-for pattern in "${GATE_OLD}" "${FLAGS_OLD}"; do
-    if ! grep -qF "${pattern}" "${FILE}"; then
-        echo "ERROR: expected line not found in ${FILE}:" >&2
-        echo "  ${pattern}" >&2
-        echo "setup_rocm.py changed upstream; re-check this patch before building." >&2
-        exit 1
-    fi
-done
-
-if ! grep -qF "${WARP_OLD}" "${UTILS}"; then
-    echo "ERROR: expected WARP_SIZE block not found in ${UTILS}." >&2
-    echo "utils.h changed upstream; re-check the wave32 fix before building." >&2
-    exit 1
-fi
-
-python3 - "${UTILS}" "${WARP_OLD}" "${WARP_NEW}" <<'PY'
-import sys
-
-path, old, new = sys.argv[1:4]
-with open(path) as f:
-    src = f.read()
-with open(path, "w") as f:
-    f.write(src.replace(old, new, 1))
-PY
-
-python3 - "${FILE}" "${GATE_OLD}" "${GATE_NEW}" "${FLAGS_OLD}" "${FLAGS_NEW}" <<'PY'
-import sys
-
-path, gate_old, gate_new, flags_old, flags_new = sys.argv[1:6]
-with open(path) as f:
-    src = f.read()
-src = src.replace(gate_old, gate_new)
-src = src.replace(flags_old, flags_new, 1)
-with open(path, "w") as f:
-    f.write(src)
-PY
-
-echo "Patched ${FILE} for gfx1151:"
-grep -nF -e "${GATE_NEW}" -e "SGL_ROCM_WARP_SIZE" "${FILE}"
-echo "Patched ${UTILS} for wave32:"
-grep -nF "SGL_ROCM_WARP_SIZE" "${UTILS}"

-# gfx942/gfx950/gfx1250 and hard-exits on anything else; the patch below lifts
-# that gate. Set to 0 to skip the AOT kernels entirely and run Triton-only.

@@ -77,22 +75,13 @@ RUN cd /sgl-workspace/sglang \

-# the arch gate sys.exit(1)s outside {gfx942, gfx950, gfx1250}, and WARP_SIZE
-# resolves to 64 on the host pass but 32 on the device pass for a wave32 part,

-# non-gfx942 TopK dynamic LDS to 40KB, which fits gfx1151's 64KB limit. The

-# clean for it. Each edit greps for the expected text first, so a rewrite
-# upstream breaks the build loudly instead of silently misconfiguring kernels.
-COPY docker/patches/sgl-kernel-gfx1151.sh /tmp/sgl-kernel-gfx1151.sh
+# setup_rocm.py accepts gfx1151, and the MoE TopK launchers pick the wave size of
+# the running device, so the AOT sources build unmodified for this wave32 target.
 
 RUN cd /sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/kernels/aot \
     && if [ "${BUILD_SGL_KERNEL}" = "1" ]; then \
          rm -f pyproject.toml \
          && mv pyproject_rocm.toml pyproject.toml \
-         && sh /tmp/sgl-kernel-gfx1151.sh setup_rocm.py \
          && AMDGPU_TARGET=${GPU_ARCH} MAX_JOBS=${MAX_JOBS} python3 setup_rocm.py install; \
        else \
          echo "Skipping sgl-kernel build (BUILD_SGL_KERNEL=0)"; \

@@ -74,15 +74,16 @@ def _get_version():
 else:
     print(f"Warning: torch.cuda not available. Using default target: {amdgpu_target}")
 
-if amdgpu_target not in ["gfx942", "gfx950", "gfx1250"]:
+supported_archs = ["gfx942", "gfx950", "gfx1100", "gfx1151", "gfx1201", "gfx1250"]
+if amdgpu_target not in supported_archs:
     print(
-        f"Warning: Unsupported GPU architecture detected '{amdgpu_target}'. Expected 'gfx942', 'gfx950', or 'gfx1250'."
+        f"Warning: Unsupported GPU architecture detected '{amdgpu_target}'. Expected one of: {supported_archs}"
     )
     sys.exit(1)
 
 fp8_macro = (
     "-DHIP_FP8_TYPE_FNUZ" if amdgpu_target == "gfx942" else "-DHIP_FP8_TYPE_E4M3"
-)  # gfx950 and gfx1250 use E4M3
+)  # every target except gfx942 uses E4M3
 
 # Dynamic shared-memory budget for the TopK kernels.
 # - gfx942 (MI300/MI325): LDS is typically 64KB per workgroup -> keep dynamic smem <= ~48KB
